correctness.rationale: Distance table and exhaustive three-type mixed-triple classification imply P3-free chosen edge family and precise original-vertex exclusions. Independent components correspond to vertex-disjoint stars and triangles. Labelled exponential enumeration uses weights (1+z), z, 3z^2+z^3, kz^(k−1), plus 2C(n,2)z² exceptions. Maximum cardinality follows from component support counts and partitions into singleton and triple blocks. Standalone BFS checks 33856 exact subsets for n=3..5, 40000 n=6 samples and complete n=6 edge-family enumeration, plus top coefficients n=3..20. Finite checks are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Publication-priority review is provisional. Full-text 2024 general-position polynomial article covers other graph families, and full-text 2019 line-graph article covers the selected-subdivision-vertex subproblem but not the mixed original/subdivision-vertex enumeration. The general characterization in arXiv:1812.08460 is prior background. Targeted published-record search found related graph/invariant results, not a statement implying the full exponential enumerator. Matching incidence-graph results remain possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently named study of vertex–edge incidence graphs of K_n could already enumerate their general-position sets.
The general 2018 clique-component theorem combined with the 2019 line-graph argument may be viewed as making some derivations routine, although neither gives the exact mixed-vertex EGF.
Only the 2026 publication abstract, not its entire text, was inspected; the abstract suggests different graph families.
Independent mathematical and priority assessment has not been performed.

value.rationale: A complete size-counting polynomial and explicit extremal multiplicities for a natural quadratically large incidence-graph family. The mixed-vertex obstruction and exceptional two-vertex term require more than the known line-graph scalar result. The resulting maximum count has a natural 1/3-block set-partition interpretation; the theorem does not merely rename a general identity.
